To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) both semantic and pragmatic aspects of the context can affect sentence processing, and that (ii) the N400 is sensitive to the conditional probability of the words in the context given the sentence.

(1) the N400 is sensitive to the conditional probability of the upcoming word given the preceding context; (2) this effect is stronger when a word is predicted to be semantically relevant than when it is predicted to be a filler word, and (3) this effect is sensitive to the degree of predictability of the word given the context.

(1) the amplitude of N400 is modulated by the conditional probabilities of the upcoming words, (2) this modulation is not due to semantic similarity, and (3) this modulation can be quantitively explained by Bayesian Pragmatic principles
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the brain processes the meaning of a sentence in the context of a discourse.
the question of how the meaning of a sentence is influenced by the preceding discourse context, and how these processes can be investigated using EEG.
the interaction between lexical semantics and pragmatic inference in the process of sentence interpretation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Bayesian Pragmatis view is supported by the data.

the N400 is sensitive to the semantic similarity between words in the discourse and the words in a sentence and that the N400 can be used to measure the degree to which the sentence fits the discourse context, as predicted by the Free Pragmatic account.

the two views of contextual influences on sentence meaning composition, the Semantic Similarity View and the Free Pragmatic view are not mutually exclusive, and that the two views complement each other.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N400 is sensitive to the conditional probability of words given a context and that this effect is not due to semantic similarity alone.
the Semantic Similarity View is supported by our EEG data, whereas the Free Pragmatic view is not.
the N400 effect is not only driven by semantic similarity, but also by pragmatic factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
both semantic similarity and probabilistic pragmatic factors affect sentence meaning composition, and the effect of the two factors cannot be separated.
the Free Pragmatic view can better predict the amplitude of the N400 in the Predictive Completion Task.
the two views are not in competition.
